Telecommunications giant MTN Nigeria has hosted Nigeria’s triumphant Under-17 women’s national football team to a celebratory reception in Lagos, rewarding the newly crowned world champions with a cash gift of ₦150 million.
The special event was held to honor the squad following their historic conquest at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, where they became the first African nation to lift the trophy after a thrilling 2–1 victory over Japan in the final.
Arriving at the MTN Plaza headquarters amid cheers and music, the players, coaching staff, and team officials were welcomed by top executives of the telecommunications company.
Speaking at the reception, the Chief Executive Officer of MTN Nigeria, Karl Toriola, praised the young athletes for their resilience, discipline, and unmatched patriotism on the global stage.
“You did not just win a trophy; you shattered a glass ceiling for African football and inspired millions of young girls across Nigeria,” the CEO stated while presenting the ceremonial cheque. “As proud supporters of Nigerian football, we are honored to reward your hard work and dedication with ₦150 million to celebrate this unforgettable milestone.”
According to the breakdown announced at the event, ₦115 million of the total sum was allocated directly to the players, while the remaining ₦35 million was dedicated to the coaching crew and backroom staff.
In her remarks, the team captain, Chidi Harmony, expressed profound gratitude to MTN Nigeria for the warm reception and generous financial reward, noting that corporate backing plays a vital role in motivating young athletes to aim for global excellence.
Head Coach Akeem Busari also commended the telecoms provider for consistently standing by Nigerian national teams through thick and thin.
The reception concluded with a celebratory breakfast, photo sessions with the World Cup trophy, and renewed pledges of support from MTN Nigeria toward the development of grassroots and women’s football in the country.
